prs.author: Epochex

prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py only exempts a field from JSON pre-parsing when its annotation is exactly `str`. For union annotations like `str | None`, a string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a serialized payload passed as a plain string parameter) gets incorrectly json.loads()'d and corrupted, since the check `field_info.annotation is not str` is True for any union containing str. (2 PRs)

For union annotations like `str | None`, a string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a serialized payload passed as a plain string parameter) gets incorrectly json.loads()'d and corrupted, since the check `field_info.annotation is not str` is True for any union containing str. prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json via a new helper, but with different scope. #3056's _is_optional_str() narrowly targets `str | None` (all non-None union args == [str]), matching the reported bug precisely, and its docstring explains why broader unions like `str | list[str]` must still be JSON-parsed (only str|None can never have a non-str member produced by json.loads). #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() instead skips parsing for ANY union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - e.g. `str | int` or `str | bool | None` - not just Optional[str]. That broader rule changes existing pre-parsing behavior for numeric/bool union members that isn't part of the reported bug: a `str | int` field receiving the numeric-looking string "5" would previously json.loads() it to int 5, but under #2032 it stays the raw string "5" and validates against the str arm of the union instead of int - a behavior change beyond the str|None corruption issue both PRs set out to fix. #3056 fixes the reported case without altering that other-simple-type-union behavior, making it the more precisely scoped patch to keep.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json via a new helper, but with different scope. #3056's _is_optional_str() narrowly targets `str | None` (all non-None union args == [str]), matching the reported bug precisely, and its docstring explains why broader unions like `str | list[str]` must still be JSON-parsed (only str|None can never have a non-str member produced by json.loads). #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() instead skips parsing for ANY union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - e.g. `str | int` or `str | bool | None` - not just Optional[str]. That broader rule changes existing pre-parsing behavior for numeric/bool union members that isn't part of the reported bug: a `str | int` field receiving the numeric-looking string "5" would previously json.loads() it to int 5, but under #2032 it stays the raw string "5" and validates against the str arm of the union instead of int - a behavior change beyond the str|None corruption issue both PRs set out to fix. #3056 fixes the reported case without altering that other-simple-type-union behavior, making it the more precisely scoped patch to keep.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the exact same conditional in pre_parse_json via a new helper, but with different scope. #3056's _is_optional_str() narrowly targets `str | None` (all non-None union args == [str]), matching the reported bug precisely, and its docstring explains why broader unions like `str | list[str]` must still be JSON-parsed (only str|None can never have a non-str member produced by json.loads). #2032's _should_pre_parse_json() instead skips parsing for ANY union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} - e.g. `str | int` or `str | bool | None` - not just Optional[str]. That broader rule changes existing pre-parsing behavior for numeric/bool union members that isn't part of the reported bug: a `str | int` field receiving the numeric-looking string "5" would previously json.loads() it to int 5, but under #2032 it stays the raw string "5" and validates against the str arm of the union instead of int - a behavior change beyond the str|None corruption issue both PRs set out to fix. #3056 fixes the reported case without altering that other-simple-type-union behavior, making it the more precisely scoped patch to keep.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py only exempts a field from JSON pre-parsing when its annotation is exactly `str`. For union annotations like `str | None`, a string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a serialized payload passed as a plain string parameter) gets incorrectly json.loads()'d and corrupted, since the check `field_info.annotation is not str` is True for any union containing str.
